packet.title: approval requirements
packet.summary: Approve or reject each requirement (R1–R6, D1–D17), one signature per sentence. You certify that the sentence says what the contract is meant to do, and that the properties listed under it are the right discharge. The property text is the proof obligation; you are not signing that text as the requirement.
packet.qualifies: A named human who did not write approval-core. Claude sessions wrote most of the specs and harnesses, so a review by Claude does not count.
why_a_day: The 23 sentences are requirement/2 in prolog/requirements/approval_req.pl. That file was written from strategy.md (the Target, sections 1–4 and 5.12) and the contract README, not from the Rust. The Prolog step machine was then written from these sentences.

Each item signs one sentence and the properties traceability.pl says discharge it. Several properties share one sentence. A low-level statement such as the add_principal post-state is a proof obligation under a sentence, not a sentence of its own.
The full packet (ui/spec-approvals-full) is a separate review. Signing a requirement here does not sign that packet.

TX-3.description: authenticate: Ok <=> predecessor = signer and key registered to signer with role; errors IndirectCall, UnknownKey, WrongRole, KeyAccountMismatch; read-only
TX-3.harness: verus: authenticate ensures auth_spec; kani: h_step_request, h_step_approve, h_step_reject

TX-4.description: request_action: exact result, error order (auth, EmptyAction, ActionTooLong, TooManyPending, LogFull), appended request recording the caller's registration id, caller key pend+1
TX-4.harness: verus: request_action ensures refines(request_spec); kani: h_step_request, h_raw_request

TR-1.description: Provenance: every proof has a prior successful request by a registered agent key and a successful approval restating the action by a registered approver key of a different account, with the agent registration continuous in between; the proof's registration ids are the registrations in force at request and approval
TR-1.harness: verus: lemma_tr1 (runs from init), lemma_reg_stays; kani: h_init, h_step_*, h_bmc_from_init

SH-1.description: Env mapping (caller, now) with pairwise-distinct context values; add_agent/add_approver pass the right role; all three owner methods pass the predecessor (DAO owner works, relayed owner signature fails)

RT-KEY.description: FC key of account a arrives as signer = predecessor = a with signer_pk = key; unregistered and cross-account keys rejected

SH-4.description: approval_requested: exactly one NEP-297 line with RequestView(r), status pending; emitted only after Ok

SH-6.description: Each change method logs exactly its one event (key_added, key_revoked with voided_pending, approval_requested, action_approved, action_rejected = returned RejectionView); new, views and failed calls log nothing

C-4.description: Each event from exactly one method; authority/proof-changing ops emit an event or carry accepted_risk (admin ops emit key_added / key_revoked since 3426c92)

RT-TRACE.description: Prolog traces + 200 random sequences replayed on the reproducible wasm equal spec.rs: results, exact messages, logs, views

TX-5.description: approve: exact result, error order (auth, RequestNotFound, AlreadyApproved, AlreadyRejected, AgentRevoked, ActionMismatch, SelfApproval, LogFull), approval recorded with the approver's registration id, log appended, agent key pend-1, proof = approval(s', i)
TX-5.harness: verus: approve ensures refines(approve_spec); kani: h_step_approve

INV-5.description: Separation of duties: approver account != agent account, on every approval and rejection
INV-5.harness: verus: full_inv (inv_req), lemma_full_inv; kani: h_init, h_step_*

INV-6.description: Approver key != agent key on every approval and rejection
INV-6.harness: verus: full_inv (inv_req), lemma_full_inv; kani: h_init, h_step_*

RT-RELAY.description: Calls through a third-party relay contract fail IndirectCall

SH-5.description: action_approved: exactly one line; data = return value = get_approval(i) at approval (revocation fields null); later get_approval differs only in agent_key_revoked_at / approver_key_revoked_at

RD-1.description: approval(s,i) = Some(proof(R[i])) iff approved; None for pending, void or unknown
RD-1.harness: verus: approval ensures approval_spec, lemma_rd1; kani: h_read

RD-5.description: Per-request and paged views agree; proof findable by request_id or approval_index

HIST-5.description: Proof stability: a published proof never changes

SH-7.description: View mapping: get_approval(s) with proof_revocations, get_approvals defaults (0, 50); get_request None past #R else every field of R[i] plus request_status; get_rejection; get_revocation = V(g); get_principal None if unregistered else account, role, registration_id, pending; get_owner; counts
SH-7.harness: near-tests/tests/shell.rs sh7_*; store_diff.rs check_views every step

SH-8.description: JSON shape: README field names of every view and event payload (incl. revocation fields, RejectionView, KeyView, KeyRevokedView, BlockTimeView), U64 strings for *_ns, numbers for ids and heights, {} or null fields give defaults, whole-args null fails (wasm wrappers: sandbox), lossless conversions

VER-1.description: Accept proofs only from get_approval at final, or action_approved logs of successful receipts with executor_id = C in final blocks

RD-2.description: Exact page: approvals(f,l) = proofs of L[f..min(f saturating_add min(l,100), #L)], no drops
RD-2.harness: verus: approvals ensures approvals_spec, lemma_rd2; kani: h_read

RD-3.description: Page arithmetic over any u64 (from, limit, count): no overflow; reads only approval_count, approved_request_id(j) in the page and request(id) for returned ids; no writes

RD-4.description: Client loop (stop on empty page or from >= count) enumerates the log exactly once, in order

RES-3.description: get_approvals(0,100) over 100 max-size proofs stays under view gas and 4 MiB return; measured about 1.30 MB (1,299,658-1,299,659 B) and about 88.3-88.4 TGas as a transaction (near-sandbox 2.13.4)

VER-5.description: Enumerate with the RD-4 loop at one block_id

INV-8.description: Registration provenance: R[i].ak = k and i >= P(k).active_from => R[i].aa = P(k).account, role Agent and R[i].agent_registration_id = P(k).registration_id

RT-SELFACCT.description: A contract on the signer's own account calling C succeeds (documents F-9)

RT-METATX.description: NEP-366 delegate action outcome recorded: IndirectCall on C for both an agent function-call key and a full-access agent key (results/RT-METATX.json)

RT-FCKEY.description: Agent FC key scoped to request_action cannot call approve or add_agent: InvalidAccessKeyError(MethodNameMismatch), not a contract panic

DEP-1.description: Code hash = reproducible build, not a global contract referenced by account id; locked at deploy (deploy + new + full-access key deletion in one tx); owner is multisig/DAO; registered keys (rebuilt from an indexer) are FC keys scoped to C ([request_action]; [approve] or [approve, reject]) with finite allowance; balance buffer. Demonstrated on near-sandbox only: no testnet deployment

VER-8.description: Per proof: archival view_access_key for the agent key at the request block and the approver key at the approval block both show a function-call permission with receiver C and the DEP-1 method names (closes F-9)

TX-1.description: add_principal: Ok(principal) <=> caller = owner, key unregistered and G != MAXU; errors NotOwner, KeyAlreadyRegistered, LogFull; P' = P[k -> (acct, role, G, #R, 0)], G' = G + 1
TX-1.harness: verus: add_principal ensures refines(add_spec); kani: h_step_add, h_raw_add

TX-2.description: revoke_key: Ok(P(k)) <=> caller = owner and key registered; errors NotOwner, KeyNotRegistered; P' = P minus k, V' = V[P(k).reg -> t]
TX-2.harness: verus: revoke_key ensures refines(revoke_spec); kani: h_step_revoke

TX-6.description: Owner never changes; owner checks compare the caller account passed by the shell (predecessor: SH-1)

HIST-6.description: Registry discipline: owner fixed; P changes only by owner Add/Revoke or the pending field on request/approve/reject

HIST-7.description: Owner operations never change requests or the log, and reject never changes the log, from any state

INV-0.description: Registry is a function: one registration and role per key (MemStore has no duplicate keys)
INV-0.harness: verus: full_inv (principals is a Map; MemStore wf distinct_keys); kani: h_store_laws_mem_law_insert, h_store_laws_mem_law_remove, h_store_laws_arr, h_step_*

C-1.description: Authority matrix: one authority per change method; owner/agent/approver method sets disjoint; no key can both request and approve

HIST-2.description: Decisions immutable once recorded: approvals and rejections
HIST-2.harness: verus: hist (grows), lemma_hist, lemma_run_grows; kani: h_step_*

TR-2.description: Each request decided (approved or rejected) at most once in any trace
TR-2.harness: verus: lemma_tr2; kani: h_step_approve, h_step_reject, h_bmc_from_init

TLA-SAFE.description: TLC: Inv (INV-3..9, INV-11..16, LEM-1/2, TR-1 provenance, RidLive, Approvable) in every reachable state and StepProperty (HIST-1/2/3/7/8/9/10, TR-2, TR-3) on every step, any interleaving of all calls by all parties

TLA-IND.description: Apalache: Init => Inv, and Inv /\ Next => Inv' /\ StepProps from any state with <= 3 requests, integers unbounded, MaxPending scaled to 2: Inv and the step properties hold at every depth

LEAN-IND.description: Lean: Init => Inv and Inv /\ Next => Inv' (TypeOK, INV-2..9, INV-11..16, INV-5r, LEM-1/2, TR-1 provenance, RidLive, Approvable) for states of every size, every MaxPending, any key, account and payload types; so Inv holds in every reachable state. TLA-IND without its bound of 3

LEAN-STEP.description: Lean: every call from an Inv state, successful or not, satisfies StepProps (HIST-1/2/3/7/8/9/10), at every size

LEAN-TR.description: Lean: over every run of any length from a reachable state, a decision is final (TR-2), Void is terminal across revoke and re-add (TR-3), request content, the log prefix, the registration counter and the revocation set only grow; every decided request has TR-1 provenance
LEAN-TR.harness: tr1_provenance, tr2_decision_final, tr3_void_terminal, hist1_run, hist3_run, hist10_run

TR-3.description: Durable revocation: a request whose agent registration is revoked while pending is never approved, even after re-registration
TR-3.harness: verus: lemma_tr3, witness_trace; kani: h_step_*, h_bmc_from_init_witness

HIST-8.harness: verus: hist, lemma_hist, lemma_run_void; kani: h_step_*

LEM-4.description: Under INV-8, liveness reduces to active_from <= id; role/account checks are redundant (F-14, the 2 equivalent mutants)

RD-7.description: request_status = Approved / Rejected / Pending (live) / Void; None for unknown ids
RD-7.harness: verus: request_status ensures, lemma_rd7; kani: h_read

INV-11.description: Live registration ids are issued (< G), pairwise distinct and not revoked

INV-12.description: Revoked registration ids are issued (< G) and each is revoked once (insert_revocation's write-once law holds)

INV-14.description: Recorded registration ids (request agent, approver, rejecter) are issued (< G)

INV-15.description: Registration accounting: #P + #V = G, so with INV-11/12 every issued registration is exactly one of live or revoked

INV-16.description: Registration binding: a live registration id recorded on a request or decision belongs to the key, account and role it was recorded with

HIST-10.description: Registrations and revocations: G grows by 1 exactly on a successful Add, V gains one entry exactly on a successful Revoke, and a recorded revocation never changes

TR-7.description: Revocation record: V lists exactly the successful Revokes, in order, each with the registration id it removed (as issued, fresh, by Add) and its time
TR-7.harness: verus: lemma_tr7 (runs from init); kani: h_init, h_step_*, h_bmc_from_init

RD-8.description: proof_revocations(proof) = (V(agent registration), V(approver registration)); under Inv each is None exactly when that registration is still the key's current one
RD-8.harness: verus: proof_revocations ensures, lemma_rd8; kani: h_read

INV-3.description: Log -> request: L[j] < #R and R[L[j]] approved with index j

INV-4.description: Request -> log: approved R[i] has index < #L and L[index] = i

HIST-3.harness: verus: hist (grows), lemma_hist, lemma_run_grows; kani: h_step_*

HIST-4.description: #R grows by 1 exactly on a successful request, #L by 1 exactly on a successful approval; otherwise unchanged

INV-9.description: Pending count: P(k).pending equals undecided (neither approved nor rejected) requests of k under its registration, <= 16 (0 for approvers); the cap bound is stepped in h_raw_request
INV-9.harness: verus: full_inv (inv_key), lemma_full_inv, lemma_approver_pending; kani: h_step_*, h_raw_request

ROB-3.description: Action length boundaries in bytes: 0, 1 (a space), 2048, 2049 and a multi-byte 2050

TR-6.description: Agent storage bound as a potential: Phi = sum over agent keys of (16 - pending) >= 0 drops by 1 per successful request and rises only on a successful approval or rejection or agent Add
TR-6.harness: verus: lemma_tr6 (per key); kani: h_step_*, h_raw_request

RES-1.description: Storage growth per op (add, revoke, request, approve, reject) computed from the Borsh layout and equal to VMLogic's metering at the worst case; measured on-chain (sandbox); 16 x B_req = 0.364 NEAR per agent key without an approver (ed25519/secp256k1; ML-DSA-65 keys are refused, SH-13)

RES-2.description: Worst-case approval_requested, action_approved and action_rejected lines (2048 escaped control bytes, 64-char accounts, ed25519/secp256k1 keys, max u64s) fit 16384 B: 13197 B (F-4). ML-DSA-65 keys, which would reach 18256 B on both sides (F-17), cannot be registered (SH-13)

SH-13.description: add_agent and add_approver refuse ML-DSA-65 keys (F-17): after the owner check (non-owners get NotOwner) and before the core's guards (LogFull), with exactly UNSUPPORTED_KEY_TYPE and no log; so every registered key is ed25519 or secp256k1, the key types RES-1 and RES-2 bound

ASM-DERIVE.statement: (M5 only) #[derive(Clone)] clones field-wise and #[derive(PartialEq)] on Role compares variants; the twin declares these for the core's data types (verus/TRUSTED.toml), which stay outside verus! so their derives are untouched

ASM-IDTYPE.statement: (M5 only) On near_sdk::AccountId and near_sdk::PublicKey, == is structural equality and clone returns an equal value (the eq_laws / clone_laws hypotheses every Verus core function requires); the equivalence half of ASM-IDENT without its parametricity half

ASM-STORE.statement: store::LookupMap is a map keyed prefix ++ borsh(key); writes flushed when the contract struct drops after state_write. For M5 path A: the contract crate's Store impl meets the Store trait's Verus contract (verified for MemStore; tested, not proved, for the NEAR store)

ASM-TOOLS.statement: Kani (unwinding assertions on), Verus+Z3, scryer-prolog, TLC, Apalache and the Lean 4 kernel are sound at the pinned versions

ASM-SPEC.statement: spec.rs, the Verus specs and the Prolog requirements state the intended behaviour; signed off by a human who did not write approval-core

ASM-STRLEN.statement: (M5 only) String::len is the UTF-8 byte length; is_empty <=> len == 0

ASM-SIGNER.statement: signer_account_pk() is the key whose signature over the originating tx was verified, an access key of signer_account_id(); signatures unforgeable

ASM-PRED.statement: predecessor_account_id() is unforgeable; equals the signer for the first receipt and when code on the signer's own account calls (F-9)

ASM-ATOMIC.statement: Atomicity is per receipt: panic, out-of-gas or LackBalanceForState reverts all writes, including earlier actions batched in the same receipt; logs of a failed receipt may remain

ASM-COMPILE.statement: rustc/LLVM/wasm-opt preserve core semantics host -> wasm32; overflow-checks on in release; the only on-chain usize use is action.len() > MAX_ACTION_LEN; cfg(feature="borsh") gates only use/derive

ASM-SDK.statement: #[init] panics if state exists; #[private] requires predecessor = current account; non-payable change methods reject deposits; &self never writes; only #[near] impl methods exported; PanicOnDefault blocks default init

ASM-FINAL.statement: State at finality 'final' is never reverted

ASM-IDENT.statement: PartialEq on AccountId/PublicKey is an equivalence matching Borsh-byte equality; the core uses A/K only via Clone and PartialEq (parametricity: a footprint maps injectively into the harness identities, ST-8W); harnesses use opaque newtypes so a new trait bound breaks the build. Which views LINK covers is no longer part of it (LEAN-COVER, K-LINK-T)

ASM-LIMITS.statement: max_total_log_length 16384 B; 100 logs; 4 MiB return data; 300 TGas per call; view gas cap per node

ASM-META.statement: NEP-366 (and NEP-518 eth-implicit) inner receipts carry the relayer as signer, so relayed calls fail IndirectCall

ASM-FCKEY.statement: Function-call keys restrict receiver and methods, cannot attach deposits, have an allowance, and cannot add keys

ASM-DEPLOY.statement: The deployed code is the reproducible build of the pin, locked at deploy

ASM-OWNER.statement: The owner registers keys honestly (it could otherwise register two accounts it controls)

ASM-MODEL.statement: Kani-layer properties only: a core step on a state larger than the Kani bound behaves like one within it (strategy section 6.3). Properties on the verus layer (M5 path A) are proved on the real core at every size and do not rely on it

ASM-TLA-SCOPE.statement: TLA+ model bounds (strategy section 17.3): behaviours with more requests, keys or accounts than TLC and Apalache explore add no new violations. Accounts and keys are covered by ASM-IDENT parametricity; the request bound is a small-scope assumption. It backs no every-size claim: LEAN-IND, LEAN-STEP and LEAN-TR prove the safety properties and LEAN-LIVE proves TLA-LIVE-1/1s at every size (strategy sections 18.3, 18.7). It remains only as the scope of the TLC and Apalache rows themselves

ASM-LEAN-TLA.statement: The Lean machine (lean/ApprovalLean/Machine.lean, Props.lean) transcribes ApprovalCore.tla and ApprovalProps.tla, and Liveness.lean transcribes MC_Liveness.tla with TLA+'s temporal operators over behaviours Nat -> State (strategy sections 18, 18.7)

ASM-STAKE.statement: Account must hold storage_usage * 1e19 yocto; ~40 B overhead per record

ASM-NU.statement: The Rust (kani/src/norm.rs) and Lean (lean/ApprovalLean/Ident.lean) transcriptions of LINK's class, representative and transport functions agree (strategy section 18.6.1)

ASM-TIME.statement: block_height and block_timestamp never decrease across receipts on one account

ASM-CODE.statement: Code changes only via DeployContract or UseGlobalContract on C (both need a full-access key on C), or via DeployGlobalContract by the owner of a NEP-591 global contract C references by account id; DeleteAccount erases state and a recreated account starts empty

F-9.finding: `predecessor == signer` also admits code deployed on the signer's own account.
F-9.resolution: DEP-1 requires registered keys to be function-call keys with receiver `C`. RT-SELFACCT.

F-14.finding: Two equivalent mutants. In `live_agent_registration`, dropping the role check or the account check survives all tests: under INV-8 both are implied by `active_from ≤ id`. They are kept as defence in depth.
F-14.resolution: LEM-4 proves the redundancy, so the equivalence is established and not merely assumed.

F-4.finding: `MAX_ACTION_LEN` is coupled to the 16 KiB log limit. The worst-case `action_approved` line is about 13.0 KB (2048 control bytes escaped to `\u00XX`, 64-char accounts, secp256k1 keys, max `u64`s). The limit breaks above about 2.6 KB. Upstream has a doc comment but no test.

F-17.finding: near-sdk-core 4.2.3 (in the lockfile) accepts **ML-DSA-65** public keys (1952 bytes; nearcore 2.13, protocol 85). With ML-DSA-65 keys on both sides, the worst-case `action_approved` line is 18256 B, over the 16384 B limit: the core accepts the request, and that approver key can never approve it (the call fails with `TotalLogLengthExceeded`). One ML-DSA-65 key on either side still fits (≤ 15775 B), so another approver with a shorter key can. Storage per request also grows (`B_req` 4160 B; 16 pending = 0.666 NEAR). The README's worst case assumes secp256k1.
F-17.resolution: **Fixed upstream** in trust-framework PR #19 (pin `081a3a6`, 2026-10-17): `add_agent`/`add_approver` refuse ML-DSA-65 keys after the owner check. Checked by SH-13 (`f17_mldsa65_keys_are_refused`). Supporting them later needs a shorter event or a lower action limit (README).

F-6.finding: `revoke_key` calls `remove_principal` before knowing the key exists. The core's "no writes on `Err`" holds only because removing an absent key is a no-op (L-REMOVE-ABSENT). On-chain the call panics before any flush, so nothing is written.
F-6.resolution: ST-2 records it. Optionally reorder upstream (OQ-5).

F-7.finding: `approve`'s `LogFull` branch is unreachable under `Inv`: a pending request implies `#L < #R ≤ MAXU`.
F-7.resolution: Kept as defence in depth. LEM-3.
